images.note: Warren G. Harding bends to greet a young girl during his 1920 'front porch' campaign, run from his Marion, Ohio home. Directly illustrates the script's 'return to normalcy' beat (61% of the vote, first national election where women could vote). Contemporary photograph, dated 1920, Ohio History Connection. Alt is null: the Library of Congress holds a Harris & Ewing Harding portrait, but only a 1024px service copy is publicly retrievable (below the 1200px bar); no second qualifying institution found.
images.title: Warren G. Harding's 1920 front-porch campaign, Marion, Ohio

images.note: State militia trucked into Union Station during the 1919 Boston police strike, photographed by Leslie Jones. Covers two script beats: the 1919 strike wave that fed the Red Scare, and Calvin Coolidge breaking the strike ('no right to strike against public safety'). Contemporary photograph, dated 1919, Boston Public Library (Leslie Jones Collection). Alt is null: no second qualifying institution found at the bar.
images.source: Boston Public Library (Leslie Jones Collection, via Digital Commonwealth)
images.title: State militia at Union Station during the 1919 Boston police strike
